:J U D G M E N T:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows: That on 11102022 at about 0900 p.m., the petitioner was travelling as pillion rider in the two wheeler motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA02KD1291 on R.V road, South end side to J C road side along with his friend Mr.Adnam Pasha who was riding the aforesaid motorcycle.

When they reached near Lalbag West Gate Signal, Basavanagudi, Bangalore at that time all of a sudden a Car bearing Reg.No.KA51MR9983 driven by its driver at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner from J.C road side in front of petitioner's vehicle and came on wrong lane, in one way and jumped the signal dashed against the petitioner's vehicle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his left leg .

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Shekhar Hospital, Bangalore wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 10 days and underwent surgery for CRIF with IMIL tibia nail done under SAB on 1310 2022.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So far the petitioner has spent more than Rs.2, 00,000/ towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and health.

He was working as stitching two wheeler sheet cover at Spliedid Flooring Mat Company and earning monthly Rs.20,
000/ per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do his occupation and earn his lively hood.
He has suffered constant pain and discomforts throughout his life.
3. In spite of service of notice, the Respondent no.1 has remained absent hence he was placed exparte.

4. Respondent No2 United India Insurance Co.Ltd., /insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51 MR 9983 has filed their written statement and contended that the claim petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties, that the accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider himself who without having proper look out over the vehicular traffic, without holding a DL and without wearing helmet was riding the vehicle, that the petitioner has colluded with the police has wrongly implicated the alleged vehicle in order to get a wrongful gain.
It is further contended that the driver of the car has also lodged the complaint against the rider of motorcycle and FIR is also registered in Cr.No.148/2022 .
It is further contended that the driver of the offending car had a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle.
05. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on 11102022 on account of rash and negligent driving of the Motor Car bearing Reg.No.KA51MR 9983 by its driver as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked in all 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral evidence.

07. Heard arguments of the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the materials placed on record.
08.

My findings on the abovereferred Issues are as under: Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : In Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

As per the final order,
 for the following.

:REASONS:
9. Issue No.1 :  In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 11102022 at about 0900 p.m. when he was travelling as pillion rider in the two wheeler motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA02KD1291 on R.V road, South end side to J C road side along with his friend Mr.Adnam Pasha who was riding the aforesaid motorcycle.

When they reached near Lalbag West Gate Signal, Basavanagudi, Bangalore at that time all of a sudden a Car bearing Reg.No.KA51 MR9983 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) driven by its driver at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner from J.C road side in front of petitioner's vehicle and came on wrong lane, in one way and jumped the signal dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and amount spent for treatment etc.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 which are the police records such as F.I.R. complaint, spot mahazar,
rough sketch, wound certificate, IMV report, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to notice, charge sheet, are the material documents to prove the present issue.

Irfan Khan vs Uma Shankar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157845924/
3 11.

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Umashankar, case has been registered against the rider/ Adnan Phasha of the motorcycle bearing No.KA02KD 1291 in Crime No.0148/2022 of Basavanagudi Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.

After completing investigation, the investigation officer filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing No.KA51MR9983/complainant for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
12.
It is relevant to state here that the rider of motorcycle has also filed claim petition before this court in MVC No.6189/2022 as he too had sustained injuries.
As per the memo filed by the learned counsel for petitioner, MVC No.6189/2022 was clubbed with present petition so as to record common trial.
Since, petitioner in MVC No.6189/2022 did not turn up to give evidence, the learned counsel for petitioner in MVC No.6189/2022 filed memo withdrawing the petition.
Hence, this court concentrates its attention only on the present application.

13. As observed in the previous para, it is on the basis of the complaint lodged by the owner/driver of the offending vehicle, case was registered against the rider of the motorcycle by name Adnam Pasha who was petitioner in MVC No.6189/2022 alleging that the rider of motorcycle jumped the signal by coming in the wrong lane and hit against the vehicle of the complainant.
Accordingly FIR as per Ex.P1 was registered against Adnam Pasha.
But during the course of investigation it was found that the driver/owner of the car was hit against to the motorcycle by jumping the signal and by coming in the wrong lane.
Hence charge sheet was filed against the driver of the complainant.
If police documents are perused, after hitting the motorcycle, the respondent no.1 tried to ran away from the spot.
But general public caught hold of him and sent the injured to the hospital with his vehicle.
In the MLC register it was clearly mentioned that the two wheeler in which petitioner was travelling was hit by four wheeler.

If the spot mahazar, sketch and other police documents are carefully perused, it clearly reveals that the respondent no.1 alone has caused for the accident, hence only even though complaint was lodged against the rider of motorcycle but charge sheet was filed against the owner of offending vehicle.
Admittedly, the owner of offending vehicle did not challenge the charge sheet.
Even before this court also though summons was served but he did not appear and contest the case and hence he was placed exparte
. If really, accident in question has not occurred due to his negligence he would have contested the case and would have given the evidence against to the case of the petitioner.
Hence, materials placed on records clearly reveal the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustaining grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P5 and ExP.11.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 12102022 to 21102022 at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Bengaluru for a period of 10 days.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Earlier to that on 11102022 he has taken primary treatment at Shekar Hospital, Bangalore.
As per wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.
15. Dr.S.A Somashekara

Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bangalore has given evidence as Pw3 and through him OPD record with examination report and Xray film are Irfan Khan vs Uma Shankar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157845924/
4 got marked as Ex.P.17 and 18.

P.W.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically as to the assessment of disability, that the petitioner has suffered disability of left lower limb at 35.55% and that of his whole body at 18%.
PW.3 further deposed that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant at both sites it would cost around Rs.40,000/ in private set up.
16. Admittedly, PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

As per the evidence of PW.3 earlier to assessing the disability of petitioner he has not collected the opinion of treated doctor and that he has only verified the wound certificate and discharge summary of petitioner and has not verified the old x rays of the petitioner.
As observed supra, as per the evidence of PW.3 the petitioner has sustain permanent disability of 35.55 on left lower limb and on whole body at 18%.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

entities.text: 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this court inclines to assess the disability of petitioner at 11% instead of 18%.
17. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
18. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/ towards pain and sufferings.

19. So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 18 medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for Rs.14,963/. But the said amount includes sum of Rs.5,000/ paid towards advance amount.
Hence, Rs.5,000/ is to be deducted from Rs.14,963/.
Under such circumstances the petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,963/ under the head medical expenses.
20. It is stated that petitioner was working as a stitching two wheeler sheet cover at Spliedid Flooring Mat Company and earning sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
To substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/ p.m.
21.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 11 days as an inpatient in Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15, 500/ p.m for three months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.46,500/ towards loss of income during the laid down period.

5 22.

sentences.text: From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment several times.
Further for 11 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022.
23.
It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 20 years.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Aadhaar card of the petitioner which show his date of birth as 30082002 and as the accident took place in the year 2022, therefore the deceased was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.

24. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/ p.m and if 11% of loss of earning capacity i.e., 1/3rd on whole body is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 20 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of to 15 to 25 is '18'.

So by applying the multiplier '18' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.3,68,280/ (i.e., 15,500 x 11%
x 18 x12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,68,280/ towards future loss of income due to disability.
25. So far as future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.3 has deposed that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant at both sites would cost around Rs.40,000/ in private set up.

Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.20,000/.
26.
The petitioner at his age of 20 years has suffered one grievous injury which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.20,000/ towards loss of comfort and amenities.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount Rs.
o.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/
 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.25,000/
 charges and nourishing food  3. Towards loss of income during Rs.46,500/
 laid up period  4. Future Loss of Income Rs.3,68,280/
 5.

Medical expenses Rs.9,963/
 6. Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/
7. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.20,000/
 Total Rs.5,39,743/

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,39,743/ (Rupees Five Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Three only).
Irfan Khan vs Uma Shankar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157845924/
6 27.

entities.text: Irfan Khan vs Uma Shankar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,39,743/ (Rupees Five Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Three only) with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.5,19,743/ from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through Epayment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 12th day of June 2024.)

ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,39,743/ (Rupees Five Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Three only) with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.5,19,743/ from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through Epayment on proper identification.
